steps.stem:
The diagonals of rectangle ABCD intersect at E. Given:
\(\begin{cases} CD=5\text{ cm} \\ \angle BEC=120° \end{cases}\)
What is the area of the rectangle (in cm²)?
explanation: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, therefore \(EB=EC\). Triangle BEC is isosceles, and its base angles are \(\frac{180°-120°}{2}=30°\).
In right triangle BCD, \(\angle DBC=30°\). CD is opposite the \(30°\) angle: it is the short leg, 5. The long leg is \(BC=5\sqrt3\) (the sides are in the ratio \(1 : \sqrt3 : 2\)).
\(S=5\cdot5\sqrt3=25\sqrt3\).

steps.stem: In parallelogram ABCD, the marked parts of angle B are \(3\alpha\) and \(2\alpha\), and the marked parts of angle C are \(3\beta\) and \(2\beta\). The segments BE and CE meet as in the accompanying figure. What is x?
explanation: Angle B is \(3\alpha+2\alpha=5\alpha\), and angle C is \(5\beta\). Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add up to \(180°\): \(5\alpha+5\beta=180°\). Therefore \(\alpha+\beta=36°\).
In triangle BCE: \(x=180°-3\alpha-3\beta=180°-3(\alpha+\beta)=180°-108°=72°\).

Shortcut · Plugging in numbers: only \(\alpha+\beta=36°\) is fixed, and the question expects one x, so any pair that fits will do. Take \(\alpha=\beta=18°\): angles B and C are \(5\cdot18°=90°\) (a rectangle — still a parallelogram), and \(x=180°-54°-54°=72°\).

ABCD is a parallelogram, and \(AE\perp BC\). Given:
\(\begin{cases} AD=24\text{ cm} \\ CD=17\text{ cm} \\ EC=16\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the area of the parallelogram (in cm²)?
explanation: Opposite sides are equal: \(BC=AD=24\) and \(AB=CD=17\).
\(BE=24-16=8\). In right triangle ABE, the sides are \(8, 15, 17\) (a Pythagorean triple). The height is \(AE=15\).
\(S=BC\cdot AE=24\cdot15=360\).

steps.stem:
ABCD is a parallelogram. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=10\text{ cm} \\ BC=14\text{ cm} \\ \angle ABC=150° \end{cases}\)
What is the area of the parallelogram (in cm²)?
explanation: The base is \(BC=14\). Drop the height from A. Angle B is obtuse, so the foot H falls on the extension of CB, beyond B.
\(\angle ABH=180°-150°=30°\). In right triangle ABH, the height AH is opposite the \(30°\) angle, so it is half the hypotenuse: \(AH=\frac{10}{2}=5\).
\(S=BC\cdot AH=14\cdot5=70\).

steps.stem: The sum of the lengths of the diagonals of a rhombus is 46 cm. The absolute difference between their lengths is 14 cm. What is its perimeter (in cm)?
explanation:
Call the diagonals \(a>b\). Then:
\(\begin{cases} a+b=46 \\ a-b=14 \end{cases}\)
Add the equations: \(2a=60\). Therefore \(a=30\) and \(b=16\).
The diagonals are perpendicular and bisect each other: the half-diagonals 15 and 8 are the legs of a right triangle. Its hypotenuse, the side, is 17 (\(8, 15, 17\)).

steps.stem:
ABCD is a deltoid. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=AD \\ CB=CD=10\text{ cm} \\ \angle ABD=45° \\ \angle DBC=60° \end{cases}\)
What is the perimeter of the deltoid (in cm)?
explanation: Triangle BCD: \(CB=CD=10\) and \(\angle DBC=60°\). An isosceles triangle with a \(60°\) angle is equilateral, therefore \(BD=10\).
Triangle ABD: \(AB=AD\), therefore \(\angle ADB=\angle ABD=45°\) and \(\angle A=90°\). It is a 45-45-90 triangle with hypotenuse \(BD=10\).
Each leg: \(AB=AD=\frac{10}{\sqrt2}=5\sqrt2\).

steps.stem: The area of isosceles trapezoid ABCD is 65 cm². DE is an altitude, \(DE=5\) cm, and the area of triangle DEC is 10 cm². What is AD (in cm)?
explanation: Triangle DEC: \(\frac{5\cdot EC}{2}=10\), therefore \(EC=4\).
Drop the height AF too. The trapezoid is isosceles, therefore triangle ABF also has area 10.
The middle rectangle AFED has area \(65-10-10=45\) and height 5: \(AD=\frac{45}{5}=9\).

steps.title: Quadrilaterals — area formulas
steps.intro: Pick the formula that matches what the question gives you.

head: Shape
Area
Remember
rows: the height, not the sloping side · angle \(30°\): \(h=\frac12\) side
even if the diagonals do not bisect each other

tips: Trapezoid: drop both heights — a rectangle in the middle, triangles at the ends. Right trapezoid: one height is enough.
Dropped a height? Look for Pythagoras, a triple, or a \(30°\)/\(45°\)/\(60°\) triangle.
Every length \(\times k\) \(\Rightarrow\) area \(\times k^2\) (diagonal \(+50\%\) \(\Rightarrow\) area \(\times2.25\)). Only the base grows? Area \(\times\) the same factor.
Rectangle with the perimeter and the diagonal: \((a+b)^2=a^2+b^2+2ab\) gives \(ab\) — or try a triple.

steps.title: Quadrilaterals — properties
steps.intro: Any quadrilateral: angles add up to \(360°\). Each name adds its own properties.

head: Shape
Sides
Angles
Diagonals
rows: equal · bisect each other · \(\perp\) · bisect the angles — all YES
equal · bisect each other — not necessarily \(\perp\), not necessarily angle bisectors
bisect each other — that's all (not necessarily equal or \(\perp\))
\(\perp\) · bisect each other · bisect the angles — not necessarily equal
two pairs of equal adjacent sides
the main diagonal bisects the angles between the equal sides
exactly one pair of parallel sides (the bases)
base angles equal · opposite angles sum \(180°\)
equal · cut each other into matching pieces

tips: Who is also who: a square is a rectangle AND a rhombus; a rectangle and a rhombus are parallelograms; a rhombus is also a kite. Down the family tree a shape only gains properties.
"Not necessarily": a property of a special shape (a square) is not a property of the general one (a rectangle).
Not sure about a property? Sketch an extreme version — very wide and very low — and look.
Rhombus: symmetric right–left AND top–bottom. Kite: right–left only.
An angle bisector in a parallelogram cuts off an isosceles triangle.
Midpoints of the sides: of a rectangle — a rhombus; of a square — a square with half the area.
Right trapezoid: always two right angles.

steps.stem: The accompanying figure shows quadrilateral ABCD. Given: angle A is 118° and angle B is 96°. Which of the following cannot be the value of α?
explanation: Call the fourth angle β. The angles of a quadrilateral add up to \(360°\): \(\alpha+\beta=360°-118°-96°=146°\).
Both angles are positive, therefore \(\alpha<146°\). If \(\alpha=146°\), then \(\beta=0°\) — impossible.
The other choices are possible: \(26°+120°\), \(70°+76°\) and \(124°+22°\) all give \(146°\).

ABCD is a parallelogram, and E lies on AD. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=9\text{ cm} \\ AE=4\text{ cm} \\ \angle ABC=72° \\ \angle BCE=54° \end{cases}\)
What is the perimeter of the parallelogram (in cm)?
explanation: Opposite angles are equal: \(\angle D=\angle B=72°\). Adjacent angles: \(\angle C=180°-72°=108°\), therefore \(\angle ECD=108°-54°=54°\).
Triangle EDC: \(\angle CED=180°-72°-54°=54°\). Two equal angles, therefore \(ED=CD=AB=9\). (An angle bisector in a parallelogram cuts off an isosceles triangle.)

steps.stem: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD intersect at E. Given: \(BC=24\) cm, and the perimeter of triangle EBC is 50 cm. What is the area of triangle ABE (in cm²)?
explanation: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other: \(EB=EC\). \(EB+EC=50-24=26\), therefore each is \(13\) and \(AC=26\).
Right triangle ABC: hypotenuse 26 and leg 24, therefore \(AB=10\) (\(10, 24, 26\) — the triple \(5, 12, 13\) doubled). The rectangle is \(10\cdot24=240\).
The diagonals of any parallelogram (a rectangle too) split it into four triangles of equal area: \(S_{ABE}=\frac{240}{4}=60\).

steps.stem:
ABCD is a rhombus. Given:
\(\begin{cases} BD=10\text{ cm} \\ \angle ABD=60° \end{cases}\)
What is the area of the rhombus (in cm²)?
explanation: \(AB=AD\) (all the sides of a rhombus are equal), therefore triangle ABD is isosceles with a \(60°\) angle. It is equilateral: \(AB=AD=BD=10\).
All the sides are 10, therefore triangle BCD is equilateral too.
\(S=2\cdot\frac{10^2\sqrt3}{4}=2\cdot25\sqrt3=50\sqrt3\).

steps.stem: ABCD is a square, and P is a point inside it such that triangle BPC is equilateral. What is angle PAD?
explanation: \(BP=BC=AB\) (the sides of the equilateral triangle and of the square).
\(\angle ABP=90°-60°=30°\). Triangle ABP is isosceles: \(\angle BAP=\frac{180°-30°}{2}=75°\).
\(\angle PAD=90°-75°=15°\). (75° is a trap: it is angle BAP.)

ABCD is a deltoid, and its diagonals meet at O. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=AD=17\text{ cm} \\ CB=CD \\ BO=15\text{ cm} \\ OC=12\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the area of the deltoid (in cm²)?
explanation: The main diagonal AC bisects BD: \(OD=BO=15\), therefore \(BD=30\).
Right triangle AOD: hypotenuse 17 and leg 15, therefore \(AO=8\) (\(8, 15, 17\)). \(AC=8+12=20\).
\(S=\frac{AC\cdot BD}{2}=\frac{20\cdot30}{2}=300\).

ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid with \(AD\parallel BC\). Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=AD=7\text{ cm} \\ \angle ABD=30° \end{cases}\)
What is its perimeter (in cm)?
explanation: \(AB=AD\), therefore \(\angle ADB=\angle ABD=30°\) and \(\angle A=180°-30°-30°=120°\).
Angles on the same leg add up to \(180°\): \(\angle B=60°\), therefore \(\angle DBC=60°-30°=30°\). The trapezoid is isosceles: \(\angle C=\angle B=60°\).
Triangle BCD has angles \(30°\), \(60°\) and \(90°\). The short leg is \(CD=AB=7\), therefore the hypotenuse is \(BC=2\cdot7=14\).

steps.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is 17 cm, and one side is 6 cm long. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: The other side: \(\frac{17-2\cdot6}{2}=\frac52=2.5\).

steps.stem: In which of the following quadrilaterals are the diagonals not necessarily perpendicular?
explanation: Square, rhombus and deltoid: the diagonals are always perpendicular.
Rectangle: the diagonals are equal and bisect each other, but they are not necessarily perpendicular. Example: a \(6\times2\) rectangle.

steps.stem: The side length of an equilateral triangle equals the perimeter of a square. The triangle’s perimeter is 252 cm. What is the side length of the square (in cm)?
explanation: The side of the triangle is \(\frac{252}{3}=84\).
This is the perimeter of the square, therefore each side of the square is \(\frac{84}{4}=21\).

steps.stem: Four squares are congruent. In each square, a route consists of four segments, each equal in length to either a side or a full diagonal of the square. Which route is shortest?
choices: Two side-length segments and two diagonal-length segments
Three side-length segments and one diagonal-length segment
One side-length segment and three diagonal-length segments
explanation: A diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose legs are sides of the square, therefore it is longer than a side (\(d=s\sqrt2\)).
Each route has four segments. Replacing a side-length segment with a diagonal-length segment makes the route longer, therefore four sides is the shortest route.

steps.stem: A square with perimeter 48 cm is divided into 12 congruent rectangles in three rows and four columns. What is the perimeter of each small rectangle (in cm)?
explanation: The side of the square is \(\frac{48}{4}=12\).
Each small rectangle is \(\frac{12}{4}=3\) wide and \(\frac{12}{3}=4\) tall.

steps.stem: ABCD is a parallelogram. BE bisects angle ABC and meets AD at E. Given: angle BCD is 136°. What is angle AEB?

steps.stem:
ABCD is a parallelogram. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=7\text{ cm} \\ BC=10\text{ cm} \\ \angle ABC=30° \end{cases}\)
What is the area of the parallelogram (in cm²)?
explanation: Drop the height from A to BC. It is opposite the \(30°\) angle in a right triangle with hypotenuse \(AB=7\), therefore it is half of it: \(h=3.5\).
\(S=BC\cdot h=10\cdot3.5=35\).

steps.stem: A parallelogram has base 15 cm and area 90 cm². Its base is increased by 20%, while its height stays the same. What is its new area (in cm²)?
explanation: The height stays the same, therefore the area grows by the same percent as the base.
\(90\cdot1.2=108\). Check: the height is \(\frac{90}{15}=6\), the new base is \(18\), and \(18\cdot6=108\).

steps.stem: The length and the width of a rectangle are each increased by 10%. By what percent does its area increase?
explanation: Every length times \(1.1\) means the area times \(1.1^2=1.21\): an increase of \(21\%\).
Check with numbers: a \(10\times20\) rectangle (area 200) becomes \(11\times22\) (area 242). \(\frac{42}{200}=21\%\).

steps.stem: An isosceles trapezoid has bases of 8 cm and 20 cm and legs of 10 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: Drop both heights. The difference of the bases, \(20-8=12\), splits into two equal ends of 6.
Each end triangle: hypotenuse 10 and leg 6, therefore the height is 8 (\(6, 8, 10\)).

steps.stem:
ABCD is a deltoid, and its diagonals intersect at O. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=AD=13\text{ cm} \\ CB=CD \\ BO=5\text{ cm} \\ OC=8\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: \(OD=BO=5\), therefore \(BD=5+5=10\).
Right triangle ABO: \(5, 12, 13\), therefore \(AO=12\) and \(AC=12+8=20\).

\(\begin{cases} AD=5\text{ cm} \\ BC=11\text{ cm} \\ AB=8\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the perimeter of the trapezoid (in cm)?
explanation: Drop the height DE to BC. ABED is a rectangle: \(DE=AB=8\) and \(BE=AD=5\), therefore \(EC=11-5=6\).
Right triangle DEC: legs 6 and 8, therefore \(CD=10\) (\(6, 8, 10\)).

steps.stem: The rectangle consists of 35 congruent unit squares. What is the shaded area?
explanation: Each white deltoid has perpendicular diagonals 4 and 2: \(S=\frac{4\cdot2}{2}=4\). The two deltoids: \(8\).
The rectangle is 35, therefore the shaded area is \(35-8=27\).

steps.stem: A rhombus has perimeter 44 cm. Which of the following lengths cannot be the length of its longer diagonal (in cm)?
explanation: Each side is \(\frac{44}{4}=11\).
A diagonal and two sides make a triangle, therefore the diagonal is shorter than \(11+11=22\). 23 is impossible.
The longer diagonal is at least the diagonal of a square with side 11: \(11\sqrt2=\sqrt{121\cdot2}=\sqrt{242}\), less than \(\sqrt{256}=16\). So 16, 18 and 21 are all possible.

steps.stem: Maya says: “Knowing a rhombus’s perimeter is enough to determine its area.” Ethan says: “Knowing a square’s perimeter is enough to determine its area.” Which statement is correct?
choices: Maya is correct and Ethan is incorrect
Ethan is correct and Maya is incorrect
explanation: Square: the perimeter gives the side, and the side gives the area. Ethan is correct.
Rhombus: the perimeter gives the side, but the angles can change. A rhombus with side 6 can be a square (area 36) or very flat (area close to 0). Maya is incorrect.

steps.stem: A congruent isosceles triangle is constructed externally on each side of square ABCD. The square has perimeter 48 cm, and each triangle has perimeter 34 cm. What is the perimeter of the resulting figure (in cm)?
explanation: The four triangles have a total perimeter of \(4\cdot34=136\).
Their bases are the sides of the square, \(48\) in total. They are inside the figure, therefore they are not part of its perimeter.

steps.stem: Which of the following statements is not necessarily true?
explanation: Every rhombus is a deltoid, every square is a rectangle, and every rectangle is a parallelogram — all three are true.
A parallelogram does not necessarily have perpendicular diagonals. Example: a \(9\times4\) rectangle is a parallelogram, and its diagonals are not perpendicular.

explanation: Drop EF perpendicular to BC. ABFE and EFCD are rectangles.
A diagonal splits a rectangle into two equal triangles: \(S_{EBF}=S_{ABE}=6\) and \(S_{EFC}=S_{ECD}=15\).

tips: Shaded-area questions: subtract the white from a shape you know, or break the shaded part into familiar pieces.

steps.stem:
ABCD is a rectangle. E lies on AD, G lies on BC, and F lies on AB. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AE=3ED \\ BG=3GC \end{cases}\)
Triangles FEG and EGC are shaded. Which of the following additional data is sufficient to determine the total shaded area?
choices: None of these data is sufficient
explanation: E and G split AD and BC in the same ratio, \(3 : 1\). So EG is parallel to AB, and it splits the rectangle into a left part and a right part in the ratio \(3 : 1\).
Let \(S_{ECD}=s\). Then \(S_{EGC}=s\) (a diagonal halves the right rectangle), the right rectangle is \(2s\), and the left rectangle is \(6s\).
FEG stands on the full side EG of the left rectangle, with its tip on AB: \(S_{FEG}=3s\). The shaded area is \(s+3s=4s\), therefore the area of ECD is enough.
The area of AFE or of FBG is not enough: F can be anywhere on AB.

steps.stem:
ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AD\parallel BC \\ AD=5\text{ cm} \\ BC=20\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
The shaded triangle ABD has area 15 cm². What is the area of the trapezoid (in cm²)?
explanation: Triangles ABD and BCD have the same height (the height of the trapezoid). The ratio of their areas equals the ratio of their bases: \(5 : 20=1 : 4\).
\(S_{BCD}=4\cdot15=60\), and the trapezoid is \(15+60=75\).

explanation: Angle sum: \(\angle D=360°-130°-\alpha-\beta=230°-\alpha-\beta\).
DE bisects it: \(\angle ADE=115°-\frac\alpha2-\frac\beta2\).
Triangle AED: \(\angle AED=180°-\alpha-\left(115°-\frac\alpha2-\frac\beta2\right)=65°-\frac\alpha2+\frac\beta2\).
Check with numbers: \(\alpha=110°\) and \(\beta=60°\) give \(\angle D=60°\), \(\angle ADE=30°\) and \(\angle AED=40°\). Only choice 3 gives \(65°-55°+30°=40°\).

steps.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 34 cm, and its diagonal is 13 cm long. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation:
Call the sides \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\begin{cases} a+b=17 \\ a^2+b^2=13^2=169 \end{cases}\)
Faster: 13 suggests the triple \(5, 12, 13\). Sides 5 and 12 give \(P=2(5+12)=34\). It fits, and \(S=5\cdot12=60\).

steps.intro: Perimeter questions with many small pieces usually need only one of these rules.

head: Situation
Perimeter
rows: sum of the pieces \(=\) original \(+\ 2\times\) each cut
Rectangular notch cut into a side
sum of the perimeters \(-\ 2\times\) each shared edge

tips: Area and perimeter are different questions: \(9\times5\) is an area, \(2(9+5)\) is a perimeter.

choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: For any quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals, \(S=\frac{d_1\cdot d_2}{2}\) — even when the diagonals do not bisect each other.

explanation: The square: \(\frac{42\cdot24}{7}=144\), therefore its side is 12.
Triangle AEC has height \(AB=12\) to the base EC: \(\frac{12\cdot EC}{2}=42\), therefore \(EC=7\).

steps.stem:
ABCD is a deltoid. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=AD \\ CB=CD \\ \angle A=3n \\ \angle C=n \end{cases}\)
Which expression equals angle ADC?
explanation: The deltoid is symmetric about AC, therefore \(\angle B=\angle D\).
\(2\angle D=360°-3n-n=360°-4n\), therefore \(\angle ADC=180°-2n\).

steps.stem: A quadrilateral is both a parallelogram and a deltoid. Its perimeter is 52 cm. Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: A parallelogram has equal opposite sides. A deltoid has two pairs of equal adjacent sides.
Together, all four sides are equal: it is a rhombus. Each side is \(\frac{52}{4}=13\).
The other statements are true only for a square.

steps.stem:
ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid with \(AD\parallel BC\). Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=13\text{ cm} \\ BC=26\text{ cm} \\ \angle BAC=90° \end{cases}\)
What is α?
explanation: In right triangle ABC, \(BC=26=2\cdot AB\). The hypotenuse is twice a leg, therefore it is a 30-60-90 triangle: \(\angle ACB=30°\) and \(\angle ABC=60°\).
The angles on leg AB add up to \(180°\), and the trapezoid is isosceles: each top angle is \(180°-60°=120°\). \(\alpha=120°\).

steps.stem:
ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid with \(AD\parallel BC\). Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=AD=CD \\ \angle DAC=2m \end{cases}\)
Which expression equals β?
explanation: \(AD=CD\), therefore triangle ADC is isosceles: \(\angle ACD=\angle DAC=2m\).
\(AD\parallel BC\) (Z-angles): \(\angle ACB=\angle DAC=2m\).
\(\angle C=2m+2m=4m\), and the base angles are equal: \(\beta=4m\).

Shortcut · Plugging in numbers: half of a regular hexagon fits every given (three equal sides, the long base parallel to the short one). There \(\angle D=120°\), so \(\angle DAC=\frac{180°-120°}{2}=30°\) and \(m=15°\), and \(\beta=60°\). The choices give \(60°\), \(120°\), \(75°\) and \(90°\): only \(4m\) fits.

steps.stem: ABCD is a rectangle. The two sloping lines meet at C and form an angle of 36°. The two angles marked α are equal. What is α?
explanation: \(AD\parallel BC\): the angle between the shallow line and AD equals the angle between that line and CB at C (Z-angles). That angle at C is α.
The right angle at C is made of α, \(36°\) and α: \(2\alpha+36°=90°\), therefore \(\alpha=27°\).

steps.stem:
ABCD is a square. Isosceles triangles AFB and AED are constructed outside it. Given:
\(\begin{cases} FA=FB \\ EA=ED \\ \angle AFB=2m \\ \angle AED=2n \end{cases}\)
Which expression equals the marked angle FAE?
explanation: Triangle AFB: \(\angle FAB=\frac{180°-2m}{2}=90°-m\). Triangle AED: \(\angle EAD=90°-n\).
The angles around A add up to \(360°\): \(x+(90°-m)+90°+(90°-n)=360°\).

Shortcut · Plugging in numbers: take both triangles equilateral, \(m=n=30°\). Then \(\angle FAB=\angle EAD=60°\) and \(x=360°-60°-90°-60°=150°\). The choices give \(150°\), \(120°\), \(30°\) and \(240°\): only choice 1.

steps.stem: ABCD is a square with side length 12 cm. Triangle AED is equilateral and lies inside the square. F lies on AB, with \(EF\parallel AD\). What is the area of the shaded triangle AFE (in cm²)?
explanation: The height of an equilateral triangle with side 12 is \(\frac{12\sqrt3}{2}=6\sqrt3\). So \(AF=6\sqrt3\).
By symmetry, E is above the middle of AD: \(FE=\frac{12}{2}=6\).
\(S=\frac{6\cdot6\sqrt3}{2}=18\sqrt3\).

steps.stem: ABCD is a square with side length 5 cm, and BEFD is a rectangle. Given: angle CBF is 15°. What is BF (in cm)?
explanation: \(BD=5\sqrt2\) (the diagonal of the square), and it makes a \(45°\) angle with BC.
\(\angle DBF=45°+15°=60°\). BEFD is a rectangle, therefore \(\angle BDF=90°\).
Triangle BDF is a 30-60-90 triangle. BD is opposite the \(30°\) angle, therefore \(BF=2\cdot BD=10\sqrt2\).

ABCD is a rectangle with perimeter 46 cm. E lies on AB, and F lies on CD. Given:
\(\begin{cases} BE=DF \\ EF=11\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the perimeter of quadrilateral AEFD (in cm)?
explanation: \(BE=DF\), therefore \(AE+FD=AE+EB=AB\).
\(AE+FD+AD=AB+AD=\frac{46}{2}=23\).
Add the cut: \(P=23+11=34\).

explanation: Push the bottom of the notch back up: the horizontal pieces still cover the width twice, and the outer sides cover the height twice. That is \(2(10+7)=34\).

steps.stem: A square of side length 12 cm has an isosceles right triangle removed from each corner. Each removed triangle has legs of length 2 cm along the square’s sides. What is the perimeter of the remaining octagon (in cm)?
explanation: Each cut takes \(2+2=4\) away from the square's perimeter and adds a hypotenuse of \(2\sqrt2\).
\(P=48-4\cdot4+4\cdot2\sqrt2=32+8\sqrt2\).

steps.stem: In rectangle ABCD, E lies on CD, and \(DE=4EC\). The areas of triangles AED, AEC and ABC are x, y and z, respectively. What is the ratio \(x:y:z\)?
explanation: AED and AEC have the same height from A, and their bases are in the ratio \(DE : EC=4 : 1\). So \(x : y=4 : 1\).
The diagonal AC halves the rectangle: \(z=x+y\).
With \(x=4\) and \(y=1\): \(z=5\). The ratio is \(4 : 1 : 5\).

\(\begin{cases} AD\parallel BC \\ AD=3a \\ BC=7a \end{cases}\)
E and F lie on BC. The area of trapezoid AEFD equals the combined areas of the two shaded triangles. What is EF?
explanation: The inner trapezoid is half of the whole area, with the same height. So the sum of its bases is half of \(3a+7a=10a\): it is \(5a\).
\(3a+EF=5a\), therefore \(EF=2a\).

steps.stem: ABCD is a parallelogram, and AECF is a square. Given: \(AD=15\) cm. The parallelogram’s area is 3 times as much as the square’s area. What is AE (in cm)?

steps.stem: Two rectangles overlap at an angle of 45°, forming the shaded parallelogram. Their widths are 5 cm and \(3\sqrt2\) cm, as marked. What is the shaded area (in cm²)?
explanation: The tilted side inside the vertical strip is the hypotenuse of a 45-45-90 triangle with leg \(3\sqrt2\). Its length is \(3\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2=6\).
The height to that side is the width of the tilted rectangle: 5.
